title: Fully differential two-stage OTA
description: The fully differential version of the two-stage Miller OTA: a differential input stage with current-source loads driving a differential common-source second stage, Miller-compensated with $C_c$ on each side. The small-signal frequency plan is the same as the single-ended Miller OTA — GBW = $g_{m1}/(2*\pi*C_c)$, an RHP zero $z = g_{m2}/C_c$ removed by the $R_z = 1/g_{m2}$ nulling resistor, a second-pole/phase-margin estimate, and a slew rate that is the smaller of what the tail delivers into $C_c$ and what one stage-2 load delivers into $C_L$. Three things genuinely differ in the fully differential form: the stage-1 load is a current source rather than a current mirror, so there is no mirror pole or pole-zero doublet in the signal path (a cleaner frequency response); the differential output swing is twice the single-ended range; and a common-mode feedback loop is needed to set the output common mode, costing supply current. As in the telescopic sheet, the CMFB loop is out of scope (no loop solving) and appears only as the current line item $I_{cmfb}$. The stage-1 output common mode $V_1$ is the node the CMFB loop holds, but it is not a free number: that node is the stage-2 gate, so the loop must hold it exactly one stage-2 $V_{GS}$ from the supply, and the sheet derives it there rather than asking for it. The first-stage current is stated the way the circuit sets it: the bias reference is programmed with $I_1$, the tail device shares that reference's gate and width, and each side of the first stage carries half of what the tail delivers, the stage-1 loads included — their gate is the common-mode feedback loop's to set, and the loop sets it so they carry what the pair hands them. The second stage carries what its load delivers: each stage-2 load is a mirror output of the same reference, on its gate at $K_2$ times its width and at its length, so the stage-2 current is $K_2 I_1$ less that mirror's drain-voltage error, and the second-stage device on each side is handed what its load delivers. The pole and phase-margin equations are ESTIMATE-grade; the simulator owns stability sign-off. On the demo NMOS table the polarity-inverted devices keep their sign params at +1.

params.name: CL
params.note: output load capacitance (per side)

params.name: Av_target
params.note: differential DC gain target: 100 (40 dB), a 1 % static error in unity feedback, is a loose floor for a general-purpose two-stage amplifier, which commonly reaches 60 to 80 dB. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: GBW_target
params.note: unity-gain bandwidth target into the 5 pF load on each side: a few megahertz is the range of a general-purpose two-stage amplifier biased at tens of microamps. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: PM_target
params.note: phase-margin target; the PM equation is estimate-grade

params.name: SR_target
params.note: slew-rate target: 5 V/us moves a 1 V step in 200 ns, in keeping with a few-megahertz general-purpose amplifier driving 5 pF. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: swing_target
params.note: required differential peak output swing

params.name: C1_est
params.note: stage-1 output node cap; refine from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis. This sheet claims no operating range: stage 1 does not close on sky130-class supplies at these defaults, and range ends that cannot be met honestly would be theater — see the single-stage OTAs for the pattern.

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the input pair's tail node. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke, and it is the tail device's drain-source voltage, so it also sets the current the tail delivers

params.name: I_cmfb
params.note: current the common-mode feedback network draws; the CMFB loop itself is out of scope — supply-budget line item only

params.name: Cc
params.note: Miller compensation cap (per side): sets the dominant pole and GBW = gm1/(2*pi*Cc)

params.name: I1
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node normally sits below the reference's diode drop), and each stage-2 load mirrors it K2:1 at the output level; the slew limits, the bandwidth and the supply current are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: K2
params.note: mirror ratio of each second-stage load, as a width ratio: each load sits on the bias reference's gate at K2 times its width and at its length, so it is a mirror output of that reference and the device that sets its side's stage-2 current. It delivers K2 times I1 less its drain-voltage error — its drain is the output, above the reference's diode drop — and the second-stage device on its side carries what it delivers. Raising it buys stage-2 slew and a higher second pole for supply current

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion

params.name: gm_id_ld1
params.note: stage-1 load inversion

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device and the stage-2 loads inherit through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node and at the outputs

params.name: gm_id_s2
params.note: stage-2 device inversion

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference, the tail device and the stage-2 loads, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirrors' drain-voltage error

params.name: V_out2
params.note: stage-2 output common-mode DC level. A common-mode feedback loop, not drawn on this sheet, holds the outputs here; this is that loop's reference

params.name: ld_sign
params.note: vds sign of the load tables: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

params.name: out_sign
params.note: vds sign of the stage-2 device table: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with the tail node as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what the tail-headroom equation watches.

params.name: Wx
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgsx
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vx
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Stage-2 current-source load
doc.description: The second-stage current-source load (per side), drawn as a mirror output of the bias reference: on the reference's gate wire at $K_2$ times its width and at its length, with its drain at the output common mode. It is the device that sets the stage-2 current, and that current is read off the table at its own drain voltage rather than typed: $K_2 I_1$, scaled by what the difference between its drain voltage and the reference's diode drop does through its $g_{ds}$. The second-stage device on its side is handed what it delivers, and its output conductance loads the second-stage gain.

params.name: Wx
params.note: the bias reference's width times K2

params.name: vgsx
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vx
params.note: the output level

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device (per side), carrying what the stage-2 load on its side delivers, at the output common mode; its gm sets the RHP zero, second pole, and nulling resistor. It is sized before the first stage, because its gate-source voltage is what fixes the stage-1 output level the rest of the sheet biases against.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-1 current-source load
doc.description: A stage-1 current-source load (not a mirror — this is what removes the mirror pole) at the stage-1 output common mode. It carries half of what the tail delivers: the common-mode feedback loop sets its gate so that it takes exactly the current the input device below hands it.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention. The parent drives it from the supply minus the stage-1 output level, which is the V1 equation's expression written out — a block's overrides are evaluated before the sheet's equations, so the level is restated here rather than referenced

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device, in one branch with the stage-1 load above it and carrying that device's current: half of what the tail delivers. Its drain sits at the stage-1 output common mode, its source one vgs below the input common mode.

params.name: vx
params.note: the drain sits at the stage-1 output level and the source at the tail node, so the parent drives this from the V1 equation's expression written out — a block's overrides are evaluated before the sheet's equations, so the level is restated here rather than referenced

equations.name: V1
equations.note: stage-1 output common-mode DC. Derived, not typed: this node IS the stage-2 gate, so the level is whatever the stage-2 device's own gate-source voltage asks for, one vgs below the supply for a p-type stage-2 (abs() keeps both table conventions working). The common-mode feedback loop is what holds the node there — it commands the level, it does not choose it, and typing a different number here is the classic way to starve stage 2. The netlist puts each stage-1 output on the stage-2 gate of its side, so the wiring check holds the stage-1 drains to this level and reports a loop that misses it

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the design constraint that places the tail node from CM_dc is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: gm1
equations.note: stage-1 (input pair) transconductance

equations.name: gm2
equations.note: stage-2 transconductance: sets the RHP zero, second pole, and nulling resistor

equations.name: GBW
equations.note: Miller-compensated unity-gain bandwidth

equations.name: wc
equations.note: angular unity-gain crossover (2*pi*GBW)

equations.name: z_rhp
equations.note: the right-half-plane zero the feedforward path through Cc would place, kept as a reference point for the UNCOMPENSATED stage: the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor below moves it to infinity, which is why the phase-margin equation carries no zero term

equations.name: p2
equations.note: non-dominant pole ESTIMATE; refine C1_est from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

equations.name: Rz
equations.note: nulling resistor Rz = 1/gm2 that moves the RHP zero to infinity

equations.name: PM
equations.note: ESTIMATE: crossover phase lag from the second pole alone, because the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor removes the RHP zero. The simulator owns stability sign-off

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the smaller slew limit: the current the tail device delivers charging Cc, or the current one second-stage load delivers charging CL

equations.name: Av1
equations.note: stage-1 gain into the input-device and current-source-load output conductances

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: SINGLE-SIDE output resistance: stage two's own output conductance in parallel with its load device's, on one of the two output branches. The differential output resistance a parent loads is twice this, the same half-circuit convention the gain and the input-capacitance equations use. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this equation is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av2
equations.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

equations.name: Av
equations.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

equations.name: swing_diff
equations.note: differential output swing = twice the single-ended range set by the two output-device saturation voltages (the fully differential swing doubling)

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact here, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the two stage-2 branches, each carrying what its load delivers, the current the tail device delivers to the first stage, and the CMFB network's budget. The reference branch that programs the tail and the loads is shared bias infrastructure, typically one reference feeding several stages, and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

equations.name: cgg2
equations.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No check reads it

checks.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target

the differential output swing meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target
